title: ExtExactFunctorCompositionComparison
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] with small Ext groups [def-pc-ext]. Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, $G:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$, $H:\mathcal A\to\mathcal C$ be additive functors preserving finite limits and finite colimits, and let $e:H\xrightarrow{\sim}G\circ F$ be a natural isomorphism. For objects $A,B\in\mathcal A$, $n\geq0$, and $x\in\operatorname{Ext}^n_{\mathcal A}(A,B)$, let $F_*x$ denote its image under the termwise exact functor on derived categories [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], using the canonical identifications of the single complexes and shifts. For a morphism $a$ write $\operatorname{mk}_0(a)$ for its degree-zero Ext class. Then
$$\operatorname{mk}_0(e_B)\circ H_*x=G_*F_*x\circ\operatorname{mk}_0(e_A).$$

source.place: Lemma Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), parts (3)-(4), and Definition Tag 06XQ (definition-ext); argument by naturality on localized complexes, written by K1

proof.text: Apply the termwise functors on complexes. Exactness ensures that each preserves quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. On complexes, applying F and then G is applying their composite, and e is the termwise natural isomorphism H to that composite. Localization carries this natural isomorphism and the composite identification to the derived categories; this is the universal property in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Both comparisons commute with shifts, since the termwise components are unchanged on shifted complexes.

Represent x as A[0] to B[0][n] by [def-pc-ext]. Naturality of the induced e for this morphism gives e at B[0][n] after H(x) equal to G(F(x)) after e at A[0]. Its components on single complexes are the images of e_A and e_B; shift compatibility makes the target component e_B[n]. These are the degree-zero classes mk_0(e_A), mk_0(e_B). Thus the naturality equation is precisely the displayed Ext equality; no sheaf, constant object or cohomology pullback is involved.

theorem exactFunctorCompositionComparison
    {C D E : Type*} [Category C] [Category D] [Category E]
    [Abelian C] [Abelian D] [Abelian E]
    [HasExt.{w} C] [HasExt.{w} D] [HasExt.{w} E]
    (F : C ⥤ D) (G : D ⥤ E) (H : C ⥤ E)
    [F.Additive] [G.Additive] [H.Additive]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits F] [PreservesFiniteColimits F]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits G] [PreservesFiniteColimits G]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits H] [PreservesFiniteColimits H]
    (e : H ≅ F ⋙ G) {X Y : C} {n : ℕ} (x : Ext.{w} X Y n) :
    (x.mapExactFunctor H).comp (Ext.mk₀ (e.hom.app Y)) (add_zero n) =
      (Ext.mk₀ (e.hom.app X)).comp
        ((x.mapExactFunctor F).mapExactFunctor G) (zero_add n)
